key_insight: Ghost tasking adds auxiliary output tasks so parametrized Gaussian Processes can be constructed even for linear differential systems that are not naturally parametrizable.
engineering_relevance: This expands physics-informed inverse modeling to harder systems with little data while keeping the number of outputs and latent functions small.
method: Introduce auxiliary "ghost" tasks to make the system effectively parametrizable.
Use the resulting parametrization to build parametrized Gaussian Processes algorithmically.
Provide computer-algebra syntax for polynomial/rational coefficients and extend theory to meromorphic functions.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports three experiments, including an inverse-problem setting, with systematic comparisons against the only other method claimed to work across all experiments.
watch_item: Effectiveness depends on constructing suitable ghost tasks and on symbolic parametrization support, which may be nontrivial for complex systems.
paper_title: Ghost tasking for parametrized Gaussian Processes solving linear differential equations
